text:
Evidence supports investigating objective alignment, but does not establish an optimal terminal-loss weight. The original [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) learns masked items using bidirectional context; inference instead predicts an appended mask. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) explicitly identifies masked-item training’s weak relationship to next-item prediction. A relevant 2024 approach, [Sequential Masked Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11150), combines sliding-window augmentation with penultimate-token masking for encoder-only session recommendation. Its reported gains concern different datasets and evaluation settings, so they do not establish improvements on this benchmark.

Practical hypothesis: retain one BERT4Rec per category and compare equal-weight training against terminal-dominant training and a gradual shift from denoising toward terminal prediction. Sample a training cutoff, supply only its preceding prefix plus the reserved mask, and supervise the cutoff item; exclude its identity and every later interaction from that input. Treat these curricula as experiments, not established findings. For auxiliary regularization, [LMA4Rec (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TKDE.2023.3330426) supports dropout-based model augmentation and contrastive learning. A small consistency loss between two dropout passes through the same terminal-prefix network is a plausible adaptation, rather than a directly validated prescription.

Prioritize terminal alignment before complex denoising: [SSDRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04278) introduces global relation encoding, augmentation and hierarchical denoising, making attribution harder. Repair diagnostic parity first: identical appended-mask construction, final nonpadding readout under left padding, and checkpoint/predictor agreement. Select changes solely through fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; no searched source establishes the winning configuration for this exact protocol.
